text:
Priya K.: Thanks folks — quick follow-up from the infra section in today's All-Hands. A few attendees asked for clarity on GPU stock levels and the autoscale behavior during region outages. Sharing notes here so we have a single thread.

Ben T.: TL;DR: we have low immediate H100 headroom in eu-west3 but healthy A10G pool in us-west1. H100 replenishment ETA depends on procurement batch (2–4 weeks). :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Sam R.: Can we get concrete fallback rules? e.g., if eu-west3 H100s are depleted, do we route to us-west1 A10G with quantized model? Or fall back to smaller model in-region?

Marta L.: Current policy is region-first fallback to compatible instance families within same region for latency-sensitive routes. If none, route-based policy can either: 1) fail fast (application-level) 2) route cross-region with lower-tier instance + quantized model. We default to cross-region only for non-SLA routes.

Eli G.: To add: we have an automatic policy flag called "prefer_local_capacity". For Hosted customers with SLO enabled, we will NOT cross-region automatically unless the route is marked "allow_cross_region_burst": true.

Priya K.: @Eli can you paste the current autoscaler snippet we showed? People asked for exact fields.

Eli G.: Sure — snippet from the playbook:

```
autoscaler:
  targets:
    - metric: gpu_utilization
      threshold: 0.7
  fallback:
    prefer_local_capacity: true
    cross_region_burst: false
    cross_region_whitelist: ["us-west1", "ap-southeast1"]
  burst_capacity:
    enabled: true
    max_extra_nodes: 10
```

Ben T.: Note: burst_capacity uses reserved spot inventory; if spots exhausted we'll try preemptible vs committed depending on tenant tier. This is why you may see short bursts that then shrink.

Olivia P.: Follow-up from product: will cross-region bursts respect data residency? We have enterprise customers in EMEA flagged as "region_locked".

Marta L.: Good call. Region-locked tenants are excluded from cross-region_burst. We added an allowlist check in the routing layer — see docs: https://redwood.example.com/docs/ops/region-locking (internal).

Sam R.: For teams: if you want to allow cross-region with quantized model, set route config: `allow_cross_region_burst: true` and `fallback_model: "gptx-small-q4"`. Ops will log an event and notify oncall.

Priya K.: Question about SLAs: if we route to cross-region and latency increases beyond SLO, does the system automatically revert?

Eli G.: Yes — adaptive rollback is active. If 95p latency breaches the configured limit for >2min, traffic will move to the next policy (usually failover to smaller model in-region or canary to a different region if allowed).

Ben T.: Action item: infra to publish a short matrix showing expected latency delta (median and 95p) for cross-region fallbacks between us-west1 <-> eu-west3 and ap-southeast1. I'll own that. ETA EOD tomorrow.

Priya K.: Thanks — one last ask from the Q&A: where do engineers put their route-level overrides? Is there a quick example?

Marta L.: Use the Console -> Routes -> Edit -> Advanced. Example payload attached in the docs: `routes/<route>/config.json` with fields `allow_cross_region_burst`, `fallback_model`, `prefer_local_capacity`.

Sam R.: @deploy-bot any scheduled maintenance in eu-west3 that could impact the H100 replenishment?

deploy-bot: Scheduled maintenance: eu-west3 kernel rollout on 1917080000 UTC. Expected 45m disruption for non-critical background nodes. Critical-serving pools are protected.

Priya K.: Great — thank you everyone. Ben, Marta, Eli — please follow up in this thread with the matrix + exact docs link. I'll summarize in the All-Hands notes. :white_check_mark:

Ben T.: Will do.

Eli G.: Adding a brief runbook for oncall to the infra wiki later today.

Marta L.: And I'll update the Console help text so teams see the fields inline.

Priya K.: Closing — if you had a question in the live Q&A that didn't get answered, drop it here and we'll triage.
